llm.summary: This skill provides disclosed, read-only access to your connected Mailchimp account using its expected authentication token.

dimensions.detail: Credential access reads the two disclosed environment variables, with no credential-file access. The configured API base receives the token; its HTTPS scheme and Mailchimp hostname are not validated by the wrapper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation declares mcporter@0.13.10 and Homebrew uv; uv runs the bundled Python server. Python dependencies use minimum versions without a lockfile. These dependencies fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions limit use to Mailchimp work. Despite missing permissions metadata, the implementation exposes fixed read operations without arbitrary commands or write tools. Interface wording mentions campaign management, but no mutation capability exists.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The server runs on demand over stdio. The bundled code creates no scheduled tasks, persistent agents, local indexes, or credential stores, and performs no account mutations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: All ten exposed tools make GET requests for Mailchimp account, audience, member, campaign, content, or report data. Sending the token as an Authorization header matches [Mailchimp's documented authentication](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/fundamentals/), rather than demonstrating credential theft.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Connect only an account whose contacts, campaign content, and reports you want the agent to read. Ensure the provisioned API base is the correct HTTPS Mailchimp endpoint, because the wrapper trusts that setting. The scanner's credential-file and exfiltration concerns are unsupported by the inspected code; authentication and network access are disclosed and purpose-aligned.
